references.text: The parallel commandment that forbids a man from lying with another man as with a woman, where the act is called an 'abomination' (תּוֹעֵבָה). This is the earlier legislation for which Leviticus 20:13 sets the penalty.
The account of the men in Sodom who wanted to 'know' Lot's male guests, something that has traditionally been understood as an attempt at homosexual acts.
The account from Gibeah that resembles the event in Sodom, where the men of the city demanded to 'know' the male guest.
Refers to cultic male prostitutes (קָדֵשׁ) in the land as part of the abominations the people practiced.
King Asa removed the male cult prostitutes from the land as part of his religious reform.
King Jehoshaphat eradicated the remaining male cult prostitutes who were left from his father Asa's time.
King Josiah tore down the dwellings of the male cult prostitutes that were at the house of the Lord.
Paul describes how men abandoned natural relations with women and burned in desire for one another, men committing shameful acts with men.
The list of those who will not inherit God's kingdom includes ἀρσενοκοῖται (men who lie with men), a term likely formed from the LXX translation of Leviticus 18:22/20:13.
The list of lawbreakers includes ἀρσενοκοῖται (men who lie with men), with the same linguistic connection to the Leviticus text.
